1d3io9h:185: Garry Tan's "skillify it" isn't just an incident response protocol—it's a human-machine collaboration language. When a temporary solution proves effective, saying "skillify it" means: turn this into a persistent capability with a SKILL.md, deterministic code, a complete test suite, and resolver entries. This protocol frees humans from "having to re-guide the Agent every time," and frees the Agent from "having to reinvent the wheel every time."
1hs6dso:275: For every 10 new skills added, there must be a DRY audit. Its core question isn't "is there duplicate code," but rather "are there overlapping trigger conditions that cause the Agent to randomly select a skill." The four Calendar-domain skills (calendar-recall / calendar-check / google-calendar / calendar-sync) are the standard example of a DRY audit: the same time domain, zero overlap, each with its own lane. If the audit finds two skills that can be merged, prioritize merging over keeping—because you can never be sure which Agent will select which one at any given moment.

5vqi53:236: The core paradox of Harness Engineering is often misunderstood in practice: adding constraints doesn't reduce the Agent's capabilities; it protects the Agent's cognitive resources from being wasted on low-value tasks. Once calendar queries are solidified into deterministic scripts, the Agent no longer needs to "think" about that problem—its attention can focus on where true judgment is required. Guardrails give people the confidence to drive 120 mph; similarly, strict skill boundaries give Agents the confidence to reason at full capacity where intelligence is truly needed. Don't avoid determinism because it "looks like it limits the Agent"—understand it as a liberation of the Agent's judgment.

q1bkyc:223: When model capabilities are upgraded (e.g., from Sonnet 4.5 to Opus 4.6), don't assume old skills are still necessary. Anthropic's approach is to remove old components one by one and test whether quality actually degrades—this should become the standard process for every Agent system upgrade. Skill decay takes three forms: Context Rot (execution quality degrades after long-running Agent operation), Data Drift (real data formats change but fixtures aren't updated), and Architectural Misalignment (model capability improvements make old constraints unnecessary). Each form requires a different remediation strategy.
v377cr:130: Unit test coverage, integration test pass rate, LLM eval scores, resolver eval coverage, smoke test pass rate—these metrics should be continuously monitored. A significant drop in any one of them should trigger an alert. This isn't the ops team's job; it's the breathing metrics of the Agent system itself.
